turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that, and on what basis.
"Get this over with." Okay. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so answer my question: on what basis, and was Owen heard before that zero went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My child never lies, and "everyone knows it" isn't evidence, Hale; who is everyone, and who else have you been discussing my son with? I'm writing down that you called Owen a cheater with no document on the table. Either you show me something with a date on it right now, or I'm going upstairs to the principal before I leave this building.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
Asking for the basis of a zero isn't bullying, Hale; it's your own procedure, section 4.3, which says software alone doesn't establish anything. I'm writing that down too. Document, or principal.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

You're the one with the evidence, Hale, and I still haven't seen any. Twenty minutes ago Owen's mark was your decision; in ten it's the principal's, and after that the board's. Last chance: what do you have?
